## 📌 Description

Provide a clear and concise description of what this Pull Request introduces, resolves, or improves. Include the context and rationale behind the change.

Fixes / Closes #(issue_number)

---

## 🛠 Type of Change

Please mark options with an `x`:
- [ ] 🐛 **Bug fix** (non-breaking change resolving an issue)
- [ ] ✨ **New feature** (non-breaking change adding functionality)
- [ ] 💥 **Breaking change** (fix or feature causing existing code not to work as expected)
- [ ] 📚 **Documentation update** (README, guides, docstrings, or lab notes)
- [ ] ♻️ **Refactoring** (code restructure without functional changes)
- [ ] 🧪 **Tests** (adding missing or updating existing unit tests)
- [ ] 🔧 **Chore / Tooling** (dependency updates, Git workflow tweaks, CI configuration)

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

Describe tests conducted to verify the changes. Include sample inputs, test commands, and environmental details:
- [ ] Automated unit tests (`python -m unittest discover tests`)
- [ ] Manual interactive validation (`python src/calculator.py`, `python src/greeting.py`)
- [ ] Edge-case and boundary verification (e.g., zero division, negative floats, empty strings)

**Test Configuration:**
- Python Version: `3.x`
- OS: `Windows / Linux / macOS`

---

## 📋 Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] My code adheres to the project's code style and PEP 8 standards.
- [ ] I have self-reviewed my own code.
- [ ] I have commented complex or non-obvious code logic.
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to documentation (`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, etc.).
- [ ] My changes produce no new warnings or regressions.
- [ ] I have added tests proving the fix or feature functions correctly.
- [ ] All existing and new unit tests pass cleanly.
- [ ] My commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) convention (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, etc.).

---

## 💬 Additional Notes / Screenshots

Add any relevant context, terminal output logs, or screenshots illustrating the change.
